member.summary: Issue #4190: retries placement tolerating a !! RUNTIME null-assertion cs2gs inserts immediately after an identifier the marked text reads — e.g. a guarded reassignment walk, current = current.BaseClass, whose receiver's nullability cs2gs's flow-sensitive analysis cannot always prove narrowed (a do/while loop's post-test guard, in particular, narrows nothing the G# binder itself recognizes — see StatementBinder.Loops.BindDoWhileStatementCore — so the bridging !! is not merely conservative there; it is required for the translated G# to bind at all), prints as current = current!!.BaseClass. Unlike (a lexical rename computed from the marked region's own syntax), the !! decision depends on flow analysis of the FULL surrounding method body, invisible from inside the marked region alone — so instead of predicting the exact re-spelling, this searches for the marked text with an OPTIONAL !! tolerated after every identifier, keeping every other character an exact literal match. The same occurrence-ordinal counted over the UNMODIFIED marker text in the clean C# source (shared with the plain-match stage above) selects which tolerant match is the right one, so a repeated marker still lands on its own occurrence.

The marker's original C# text.

member.name: M:Cs2Gs.Translator.Loading.CSharpProjectLoader.CreateWorkspace
member.summary: Creates the every design-time project load in this class uses. Issue #4278: under CI (ContinuousIntegrationBuild true, e.g. the self-migration nightly, which sets GITHUB_ACTIONS) the SDK's default targets turn on DeterministicSourcePaths, which requires @(SourceRoot) to resolve to a git repository. A throwaway fixture .csproj written under a scratch/test-output directory (or, worse, one loaded from inside the self-migration mirror, which has no .git by design — see RepositoryFileInventory) inherits this repo's root Directory.Build.props (SourceLink + git-versioning package references) via MSBuild's normal upward search, but has no git root to resolve against, and the design-time build fails outright with CS2GS0001: SourceRoot items must include at least one top-level (not nested) item when DeterministicSourcePaths is true instead of loading. This loader only ever READS a project's syntax/semantics for translation — it never persists a deterministic PathMap-mapped build output — so forcing the CI flag off for the load is safe and has no effect on any real build.

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Translator.Analyzers.SnippetTranslator
member.summary: Translates a C# analyzer-test snippet — a self-contained compilation unit annotated with [|…|] expected-diagnostic markers — into the equivalent G# snippet with the markers re-placed (docs/cs2gs-analyzer-translation.md §Test-harness). Markers are re-placed by ordered exact-text match: analyzer-test markers overwhelmingly wrap expressions whose surface text survives translation verbatim. A marker whose text does not survive is dropped from the output and surfaced as a CS2GS-ANALYZER-SNIPPET warning — loud, never silently misplaced — for the human to re-place during review. Re-placed markers denote expected-diagnostic REGIONS: G#'s syntax shapes differ (e.g. its index node is narrower than C#'s element access), so migrated verifications should assert the diagnostic starts within the marker, or hand-tighten the span during review.

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Translator.Loading.NerdbankGitVersioningPolicy
member.summary: Policy for the Nerdbank.GitVersioning (nbgv) package during migration (issue #2225). nbgv only generates the ThisAssembly source for the languages its MSBuild <Language> switch supports; G# support first shipped in 3.11.13-beta. A C# project that references an older nbgv will, once migrated to G#, silently fail to produce ThisAssembly. cs2gs therefore bumps a below-floor nbgv reference up to the minimum G#-capable version when it can do so safely (a plain literal version — never an MSBuild property, floating range, or wildcard).

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Translator.Loading.NuGetAuditAdvisoryPolicy
member.summary: Issue #2321: records every warning-or-worse line MSBuild logs while opening a project as a — including the non-fatal NuGet audit vulnerability advisories NuGet emits as warnings NU1901 (low), NU1902 (moderate), NU1903 (high), and NU1904 (critical) per https://learn.microsoft.com/nuget/reference/errors-and-warnings/nu1901-nu1904. A package flagged by one of those carries a known vulnerability but still restores and builds; it must not make gate the project out with (CS2GS0001).
member.remarks:
This policy recognizes ONLY that one stable advisory message shape as benign. It intentionally does not match:
NU1900 (a failure to even fetch vulnerability data, or a source that returned an out-of-band
severity value such as "unknown" — see https://learn.microsoft.com/nuget/reference/errors-and-warnings/nu1900): these mean the audit itself is unreliable, not that a benign advisory was found, and must stay fatal.
Genuine MSBuild workspace load failures — missing SDK/imports, an unresolvable ProjectReference,
an unsupported target framework, etc.
A mixed or multiline diagnostic message where any non-blank line is not itself an advisory: every
line must independently match, or the whole message is treated as fatal.
